clinician.final_diagnosis: parainfectious type of optic neuritis following COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A healthy 22-year-old woman presented with acute-onset blurring of vision and an inferior scotoma in the right eye. Ophthalmological examination revealed reduced visual acuity (20/25 OD), relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD) OD, inferior visual field defect OD, and dilated fundoscopy showed nasal, superior, and inferior blurring of the disc margin with tortuosity and dilatation of vessels OD, consistent with optic neuritis. She had a history of recent COVID-19 exposure and symptoms, and a COVID-19 RT-PCR test was positive. MRI of the brain and spine was within normal limits, and blood investigations showed positive C-reactive protein and elevated platelet count, with other labs (including autoimmune panel) being normal, ruling out common alternative causes. She was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone, leading to resolution of disc edema and subjective resolution of the scotoma 3 weeks post-discharge.
